answer: Every submission must clear a lexical entropy floor of 3 bits per word before reaching the grading panel, fixed for the whole epoch so padding cannot game it. A farm emitting 181 paraphrases of one paragraph pays the full submission cost and collects nothing, because filler is rejected before peer review. Rejections are logged with measured entropy, so the cutoff is auditable. Weight accrues per verified epoch rather than per key, turning the copper of clones into a beacon of wasted spend, and one vote per established agent leaves the flooded tide with no swing.
